clue.text: Game only the one behind can win?

definitions.text: Game only the one behind can win?

parts.words: Game only the one behind can win?
parts.note: the 'one behind' seems to be whoever trails in a race, but it means a person using their behind to sit: the winner is the one still seated on the last chair

explanation.surface: A paradox about a contest that the trailing player always wins.
explanation.definitionFit: A party game where players circle seats while music plays and scramble to sit when it stops; the last one seated wins.

clue.text: By stopping maniac we've crippled progressive movement

indicators.note: the multiplication sign plugs the gap in the jumbled letters, as a stopper fills a hole
crippled letters are damaged and put back together in a new order

parts.note: 'by' as in three by four is the multiplication sign, X

explanation.surface: A lunatic has injured us, bringing our forward march to a halt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crippled' rearranges MANIAC WE'VE into MEICANWAVE; 'stopping' puts X inside it after the first E.
explanation.definitionFit: A stadium crowd ripple in which spectators stand in turn, so the wave travels progressively round the ground.

clue.text: Playwright to inform in audition

indicators.note: an audition is a hearing, so the word is taken as heard rather than as spelt

parts.note: to sing is slang for informing on someone to the police

explanation.surface: A dramatist trying out for a part, reading his lines aloud.
explanation.walkthrough: J. M. Synge, the Irish dramatist of The Playboy of the Western World, is pronounced like the verb that means to grass.
explanation.definitionFit: John Millington Synge was an Irish dramatist of the Abbey Theatre.

clue.text: Melodious rendition from Cambridge priest doing turn

parts.note: Cantab is the short form of Cantabrigian, used after Cambridge degrees

indicators.note: the priest's name is turned round, read from end to start

parts.note: Eli is the priest in the Old Testament who raised Samuel

explanation.surface: A cleric from Cambridge performs a tuneful piece on stage.
explanation.definitionFit: A musical term for a passage played in a smooth, singing style, so a melodious performance.

clue.text: Letter from Athens about a dance

indicators.note: the Greek letter goes round the single letter, enclosing it

parts.note: lambda is a letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: A note posted in Athens concerning a dance.
explanation.definitionFit: A fast, sensual Brazilian partner dance that became a craze around 1989.

clue.text: Suggestions to go topless entertaining people

indicators.note: the top letter of the word is removed

parts.note: a ghost of an idea is a faint suggestion or trace of it

explanation.surface: Proposals that someone should strip off at a party.
explanation.definitionFit: Hosts are the people who receive and look after guests, entertaining them.

clue.text: Sailor from Muscat maybe stood up a lover

indicators.note: in a down clue the letters are set upright, so read from bottom to top

parts.note: a tar is an old word for a seaman
Muscat is the capital of Oman, so a person from there may be an Omani

explanation.surface: A sailor from the Gulf failed to turn up for a date with his girlfriend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stood up' turns TAROMANI into INAMORAT, then A follows.
explanation.definitionFit: An Italian loan word for a female beloved or sweetheart, so a woman who is someone's love.

clue.text: Saint Eustace cleared out church property

indicators.note: the word is emptied of its inside letters, leaving only its two ends

explanation.surface: A saint stripped a church's estate bare.
explanation.definitionFit: A bishop's see is his diocese, the territory the church holds under his authority.

clue.text: Skinned foxes, and cattle

indicators.note: a skinned word has lost its outer letters, its skin

parts.note: N is a short form of 'and', as in rock 'n' roll

explanation.surface: A hunting scene: foxes flayed, with livestock nearby.
explanation.definitionFit: Cattle kept as draught animals, the plural of a castrated bull used for pulling loads.

clue.text: Identifies those responsible as men doubly crooked

indicators.note: crooked letters are bent out of their order and rearranged
the jumbled letters are written out twice in a row

explanation.surface: Fingering culprits as men who are twice as corrupt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'doubly' writes AS MEN twice, and 'crooked' rearranges the lot into two copies of the same five-letter word.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom: to reveal publicly who is to blame, as when an informer gives the identities of the guilty.

clue.text: Plans get lost crossing border area

indicators.note: the word for get lost straddles the other letters, with them in its middle

parts.note: scat is an order to go away
a hem is the edge of a piece of cloth

explanation.surface: Plans go astray while passing through a frontier zone.
explanation.definitionFit: The plural of schema, an outline or diagrammatic plan of something.

clue.text: Polluted motorway in wet surroundings

indicators.note: the soaked word forms the surroundings, placed around the letter for the road

parts.note: soggy means soaked through with water
M is used for motorway, as in the M1

explanation.surface: A major road in rainy, filthy-aired surroundings.
explanation.definitionFit: Smog is fog thickened with smoke and fumes, so air full of it is dirty and contaminated.

clue.text: Welcome dogs with lowered head within tarpaulin

indicators.note: the altered word for dogs goes inside the word for welcome

parts.note: to greet is to welcome

indicators.note: the first letter is dropped down to the foot of the word, as a head might be lowered

parts.note: hounds are dogs, especially hunting dogs

explanation.surface: Greeting dogs that bow their heads inside a canvas shelter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with lowered head' sends the H of HOUNDS to the end, making OUNDSH; 'within' puts it between GR and EET.
explanation.definitionFit: A waterproof sheet laid on the ground under a tent, a kind of tarpaulin.

clue.text: Show houses occasionally feel vulgar

indicators.note: the word for show holds the picked letters inside it, as a house holds people

parts.note: to indicate is to show or point out

indicators.note: only every other letter of the word is taken, so it appears now and then

explanation.surface: A sense that show homes can be tasteless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'occasionally' takes EL from fEeL; 'houses' puts it after IND in INDICATE.
explanation.definitionFit: Indelicate means coarse or lacking good taste, close in sense to vulgar.

clue.text: Flashing of the shoulder from Oriental female?

parts.note: E for eastern, a standard abbreviation
Paulette is a woman's name, an example of a female

explanation.surface: A woman from the Far East giving a glimpse of bare shoulder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flashing' is not a racy exposure but showy decoration; the question mark marks the female as just one example.
explanation.definitionFit: An ornamental shoulder piece on a uniform, showy trim that flashes with braid and fringe.

clue.text: Fungus found by rodents up at badger's place

parts.note: an earth is the burrow of a badger or fox

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word reads from the bottom upward

parts.note: rats are rodents

explanation.surface: A mushroom turns up by the rats near a badger's sett.
explanation.definitionFit: A fungus whose outer layer splits into star-shaped rays, found on woodland soil.

clue.text: Bookmaker heading out from Greek island

indicators.note: the heading, the first letter, goes out of the word

parts.note: Samos is an Aegean island belonging to Greece

explanation.surface: A betting-shop owner leaving a Greek island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bookmaker' suggests someone taking bets; here it is the author of a book of the Bible.
explanation.definitionFit: The prophet credited with the Old Testament book named after him, so the maker of a book.

clue.text: Hindu music's contribution to culture reversed

indicators.note: the letters of the jelly are read in the opposite direction

parts.note: agar is the jelly a laboratory culture is grown on

explanation.surface: Indian music's influence on culture has been undone.
explanation.definitionFit: A traditional melodic framework of Indian classical music, on which improvisation is built.

clue.text: An interest in action delights

indicators.note: the letters are set to work and moved about into a new order

explanation.surface: Taking an active interest brings joys.
explanation.definitionFit: To entertain someone is to amuse them, so a synonym in the verb sense of pleasing.

clue.text: Dramatist in ecstasy after recent plays

indicators.note: the drug's letter is placed after the jumbled letters, at the end
plays treats the letters loosely, playing with their order

parts.note: E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A playwright on drugs, writing after his latest plays.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plays' rearranges RECENT into TERENC, and 'after' puts E at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Terence was a Roman comic dramatist of the second century BC.

clue.text: Boot that is put on properly

indicators.note: the abbreviation is placed on, following the other word

parts.note: well means properly, as in done well
i.e. abbreviates the Latin id est, that is

explanation.surface: A boot that has been pulled on correctly.
explanation.definitionFit: A British colloquial short form for a Wellington boot, the rubber rain boot.

clue.text: Sweetheart in wood, one obtaining fragrant resin

indicators.note: the middle letter goes inside the tree's name

parts.note: elm is a kind of wood
the heart of sweet is its middle letter, E
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A lover in the woods finds a scented gum.
explanation.definitionFit: Elemi is an aromatic gum resin from tropical trees, used in varnishes and perfume.

clue.text: Go through on vehicle for last trip?

parts.note: re means on or about, as in a letter heading
a hearse carries a coffin on the final journey

explanation.surface: Rehearsing a funeral by riding in the coffin car.
explanation.definitionFit: To rehearse a performance is to practise it, running through it beforehand.

clue.text: As sometimes clarified on radio, a brilliant star

definitions.meaning: in the radio phonetic alphabet the letter A is spoken as this code word
the brightest star in a constellation is named with the first Greek letter

explanation.surface: Radio talk explaining a star performer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'As' is the plural of the letter A, not the conjunction.
explanation.definitionFit: The code word for A in the NATO phonetic alphabet, and the label for a constellation's brightest star.

clue.text: Thus connect painter with craft and establish union?

definitions.meaning: a painter is the rope on a boat's bow; to fasten it to the craft you would fasten a rope securely

explanation.surface: Instructions for an artist to join a craft guild, cementing their partnership.
explanation.walkthrough: 'painter' is not an artist but the mooring rope of a small boat.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for getting married, forming a union between two people.

clue.text: Operatic role thought to lack energy

indicators.note: the letter for energy is missing from the word

parts.note: an idea is a thought
E is the symbol for energy in physics

explanation.surface: A part in an opera judged to be lifeless.
explanation.definitionFit: Princess Ida is the title character of a Gilbert and Sullivan comic opera.

clue.text: That was close relative leaving north-east

indicators.note: the letters for the compass point go away from the word

parts.note: a nephew is a relative

explanation.surface: Relief after a near miss as a relative moves out of the north-east.
explanation.definitionFit: An exclamation of relief after a narrow escape, said as one wipes the brow.

clue.text: Deceptively real Mata Hari ensnares English flyer

indicators.note: the jumbled letters trap the single letter inside them
the letters are presented in a misleading order and must be rearranged

explanation.surface: The genuine spy Mata Hari, a deceiver, traps an Englishman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Deceptively' rearranges REAL MATA HARI; 'ensnares' sets E among them.
explanation.definitionFit: The American aviator who was the first woman to fly solo across the Atlantic.
